claim: The spring election is held on the first Tuesday in April and elects judicial, educational and municipal officers and nonpartisan county officers
quote: means the election held on the first Tuesday in April to elect judicial, educational and municipal officers, nonpartisan county officers and sewerage commissioners

claim: The spring primary is a nonpartisan primary on the third Tuesday in February
quote: means the nonpartisan primary held on the 3rd Tuesday in February to nominate nonpartisan candidates to be voted for at the spring election

claim: The general election is held in November of even-numbered years and elects county officers other than supervisors and county executives
quote: and county officers other than supervisors and county executives

claim: The general election is held on the Tuesday after the first Monday in November of even-numbered years
quote: means the election held in even-numbered years on the Tuesday after the first Monday in November

claim: District attorneys are elected at the November general election
quote: state senators, representatives to the assembly, district attorneys

claim: State law classes the district attorney as a state office, though it is elected countywide
quote: state senator, state representative to the assembly and district attorney

claim: The partisan primary is held on the second Tuesday in August
quote: means the primary held the 2nd Tuesday in August to nominate candidates to be voted for at the general election

claim: The partisan primary nominates party candidates for national, state and county offices, each party having its own ballot
quote: the following ballot shall be provided for the nomination of candidates of recognized political parties for national, state and county offices

claim: At the partisan primary the voter picks a party in secret and cannot vote for candidates of more than one party
quote: the elector may secretly select the party for which he or she wishes to vote

claim: Votes cast in more than one party's primary are not counted
quote: the elector cannot vote for candidates of more than one party, whenever the restriction applies

claim: Plurality wins: the candidate with the most votes is elected
quote: The person receiving the greatest number of legal votes for the office shall be declared elected

claim: The general election laws apply to all elections, including local ones
quote: The general provisions of chs. 5 to 12 apply to all elections.

claim: Spring election ballots for county executive and county supervisor carry no party designation
quote: No party designation may appear on the official ballot.

claim: City ballots carry no party designation
quote: No party designation shall appear on the official ballot for city offices.

claim: Town and village candidates are nominated by caucus or nomination papers under a single nonpartisan section
quote: Every candidate for an elective office in a town or village shall be nominated under this section.

claim: Where a caucus is used, it is held in January and nominates the top two candidates for each office
quote: When nomination papers are not used, there shall be a caucus to nominate candidates.

claim: Spring election candidates are nominated by nomination papers, and by a primary if one is held
quote: shall be nominated by nomination papers, or by nomination papers and selection at the primary if a primary is held

claim: A city may hold a spring primary; there is none when candidates do not exceed twice the seats
quote: When the number of candidates for any city office does not exceed twice the number to be elected to the office, no primary may be held for the office

claim: A city may require a primary by charter ordinance whenever three or more candidates file
quote: Any city may provide by charter ordinance, under s. 66.0101 , that whenever 3 or more candidates file nomination pa

claim: Independent nominations may be made for any office voted on at the general election, by nomination papers
quote: Independent nominations may be made for any office to be voted for at any general or partisan special election.

claim: A signer of an independent's nomination paper declares they have not signed for another candidate for the same office
quote: I have not signed the nomination paper of any other candidate for the same office at this election.

claim: A person who files as a party candidate cannot also file as an independent for the same office at the same election
quote: may not file nomination papers as an independent candidate for the same office at the same election

claim: If a person signs nomination papers for two candidates for the same office, only the earlier signature counts
quote: the earlier signature is valid and the later signature is invalid

claim: School boards are elected at the spring election, by plurality, for three-year terms by default
quote: The regular terms of school board members shall be 3 years

claim: School board members are elected by plurality
quote: by a plurality vote of the electors of the school district

claim: Wisconsin is divided into the counties named in s. 2.01: 71 numbered entries plus Menominee at (39m), 72 in all
quote: The state is divided into the counties hereinafter named

claim: Menominee County consists of one town
quote: The county of Menominee consists of one town, known as the town of Menominee.

claim: In a county with only one town, the county board is the town board plus one supervisor from each village
quote: the board shall consist of the members of the town board and one supervisor from every village

claim: County supervisors serve two-year terms elected in April of even-numbered years
quote: Supervisors are county officers, shall be elected for 2-year terms at the election to be held on the first Tuesday in April in even-numbered years

claim: A county board may organize itself by ordinance and choose concurrent or staggered two-year terms
quote: A board may determine whether the terms shall be concurrent or staggered.

claim: County board size has a population-based ceiling outside Milwaukee County: at most 47, 39, 31 or 21 supervisors
quote: Counties with a population of less than 25,000 and containing more than one town shall have no more than 21 supervisors.

claim: In Milwaukee County (population 750,000 or more), supervisors are elected for two-year terms
quote: For an election that is held in 2016 and thereafter, supervisors shall be elected for 2-year terms

claim: A county of 750,000 or more must elect a county executive for a four-year term at the spring election
quote: In each county with a population of 750,000 or more, a county executive shall be elected for a 4-year term

claim: Smaller counties may create or abolish an elected county executive
quote: Counties with a population of less than 750,000 may by resolution of the board or by petition and referendum create the office of county executive

claim: Smaller counties may instead appoint a county administrator
quote: The county administrator shall be appointed by majority vote of the board.

claim: Register of deeds, county clerk and county treasurer are elected at the general election for four-year terms
quote: a register of deeds, county clerk, and county treasurer shall be chosen at the general election by the electors of each county for the term of 4 years

claim: The sheriff is elected at the general election for a four-year term
quote: a sheriff shall be chosen at the general election by the electors of each county for the term of 4 years

claim: The clerk of circuit court is elected at the general election for a four-year term
quote: a clerk of circuit court shall be chosen at the general election for the term of 4 years

claim: Counties of 750,000 or more elect a comptroller at the spring election and elect no surveyor or coroner
quote: a comptroller shall be chosen at the spring election by the electors of each county having a population of 750,000 or more

claim: Coroners are elected only where a county has a coroner, not in counties of 750,000 or more or with a medical examiner
quote: No coroner shall be elected in counties having a population of 750,000 or more or in counties in which a medical examiner system is instituted.

claim: Counties have administrative home rule, limited by statewide enactments that uniformly affect every county
quote: Every county may exercise any organizational or administrative power, subject only to the constitution and to any enactment of the legislature which is of statewide concern and which uniformly affects every county.

claim: The constitution lets the Legislature provide for an elected county executive once every four years
quote: the election at large once in every 4 years of a chief executive officer in any county

claim: Sheriffs are elected by county voters for four-year terms under the constitution
quote: sheriffs shall be chosen by the electors of the respective counties

claim: Towns elect a three-member town board in April of odd-numbered years, one designated chairperson
quote: One of the supervisors shall be designated on the ballot as town board chairperson.

claim: Towns elect officers at the annual spring election in odd-numbered years
quote: At the annual spring election in odd-numbered years, each town shall elect:

claim: Town clerk and treasurer may be made appointed offices by ordinance approved at referendum
quote: An ordinance enacted under par. (a) may not take effect until it is approved in a referendum

claim: A town board with village powers may grow to five supervisors; a town of 2,500 or more may have a five-member board if the town meeting directs
quote: Any town board authorized to exercise village powers may, by ordinance, increase the number of supervisors to no more than 5.

claim: Villages elect a president, clerk, treasurer and others at the spring election in odd-numbered years
quote: At the annual spring election in each village in odd-numbered years, except as otherwise provided herein, there shall be chosen: A president

claim: Villages in Milwaukee County (750,000 or more) elect those officers in even-numbered years
quote: In villages in counties having a population of 750,000 or more, the officers named shall be elected for a term of 2 years on the first Tuesday of April of each even-numbered year.

claim: Villages have six trustees with two-year terms, three elected each year (two trustees in villages of 350 or less)
quote: Villages shall have 6 trustees, except as provided otherwise in sub. (3) , whose term of office shall be 2 years, 3 of whom shall be elected each year.

claim: A village may change its number of trustees by ordinance
quote: Any village may by ordinance change the number of trustees

claim: Cities fall into four classes by population
quote: Cities of 150,000 population and over shall constitute 1st class cities.

claim: A city changes class only when census, government changes and a mayoral proclamation all occur, so population alone does not set class
quote: when a proclamation of the mayor, declaring the fact, is published according to law

claim: A statutory reference to a class of city does not include a city that is merely eligible by population
quote: such reference does not include any city with a population which makes the city eligible to be in that class

claim: The mayor and alderpersons are elected by the voters; other city officers may be appointed or elected
quote: The mayor and alderpersons shall be elected by the voters.

claim: General charter law provides two alderpersons per aldermanic district, which a city can reduce to one by charter ordinance
quote: provide that there shall be one alderperson from each aldermanic district

claim: City elective officers serve two-year terms unless a charter ordinance sets a different tenure
quote: Except as otherwise specially provided the regular term of elective officers shall be 2 years. A different tenure for such officers or any of them may be provided by charter ordinance.

claim: A city council can split alderpersons into two classes, after which their terms are four years
quote: thereafter the term of alderpersons shall be 4 years

claim: Cities and villages have constitutional home rule over local affairs, subject to statewide-concern laws that apply uniformly
quote: may determine their local affairs and government, subject only to this constitution and to such enactments of the legislature of statewide concern as with uniformity shall affect every city or every village

claim: Home rule is exercised by charter ordinance, which needs a two-thirds vote and is subject to referendum
quote: requires a two-thirds vote of the members-elect of the legislative body of the city or village, and is subject to referendum

claim: The Legislature convenes on the first Monday of January in odd-numbered years
quote: The legislature shall convene in the capitol on the first Monday of January in each odd-numbered year, at 2 p.m.

claim: The Legislature meets annually, and the regular session begins on the first Tuesday after 8 January unless the work schedule provides otherwise
quote: The regular session of the legislature shall commence at 2 p.m. on the first Tuesday after the 8th day of January in each year

claim: Bills not acted on in the odd-numbered year carry over to the even-numbered year
quote: shall carry over to the regular annual session held in the even-numbered year

claim: The Legislature meets when the law provides, and the governor may call special sessions
quote: The legislature shall meet at the seat of government at such time as shall be provided by law, unless convened by the governor in special session

claim: The governor has 6 days, Sundays excepted, after a bill is presented; final adjournment that prevents return kills the bill
quote: Any bill not returned by the governor within 6 days (Sundays excepted) after it shall have been presented to the governor shall be law

claim: An act with no stated effective date takes effect the day after publication
quote: shall take effect on the day after its date of publication

claim: In first class cities the school board (board of school directors) has an at-large seat on the city ballot and district seats on a separate ballot
quote: In 1st class cities, the names of the candidates for the seat of the member elected at-large to the board of school directors shall be placed on the official city ballot

claim: Act 126 (2025) requires circulators of nomination papers to be Wisconsin electors
quote: who is a qualified elector of this state shall be appended to each nomination paper

claim: The 750,000-population county rules are the Milwaukee County rules
quote: Milwaukee County. In each county with a population of at least 750,000:

claim: A town is designated by its name as "Town of ..."
quote: A town shall be designated in all actions and proceedings by its name

claim: A county not divided into towns is treated as one town, so county land outside cities and villages is town territory
quote: If a county is not divided into towns, it shall, for purposes of town government, be considered one town.
